# Saakshi Medtech and Panels Limited | Deep research, v3.0

## 1. Executive Verdict

Saakshi is principally an OEM control-panel and mechanical-assembly manufacturer, not a predominantly medical-device business. FY2026 revenue recovered to ₹115.51 crore and core EBITDA to ₹22.22 crore, but sales remain below FY2023 while manufacturing capital has expanded substantially. The ₹377 last observed traded close, dated16 October rather than the19 October market cutoff, implies about ₹741.4 crore equity value on the enlarged share count. A material minority acquisition was paid for with shares, not cash. Capital efficiency, the target’s audited economics, historical cash-flow discrepancies and practical exit liquidity remain unresolved. Classification: Hold — unresolved; a conditional turnaround/capital-allocation special situation, not an evidence-backed compounder. A verified, self-funding plant ramp and a defensible acquisition return would change the business assessment; a lower price alone would not clear the evidence holds. [E01–E05, E09–E13]

Zero turnover and volume are assigned solely for a conservative capacity calculation, not reported as observed trades; the stale quote is explicitly retained only as a valuation reference. Current issued shares are19,666,259, not17,656,000. The current600-share lot costs ₹226,200. [S17–S18]
- Financial perimeter: standalone Accounting Standards under the Companies (Accounting Standards) Rules, commonly Indian GAAP/AS, not assumed Ind AS. There were no subsidiaries in the March2026 accounts. The post-year-end acquisition is a minority stake, not permission to consolidate the target’s revenue, debt or cash. [S01, S06–S09]

Entry and exit cost assumptions are2% each, with0%/5% sensitivities.

Overall conclusion confidence is Low, determined by the weakest material subject rather than an average. Unmodified audits do not remove all uncertainty; unavailable evidence is not proof of wrongdoing. [E01–E16]

## 4. Business Overview

Saakshi designs and manufactures electrical control panels, mechanical assemblies, wire harnesses and some medical-related equipment/components. Customers buy qualified, application-specific manufacturing rather than a consumer brand. Engineering, fabrication, assembly, testing and dependable delivery matter, while raw-material procurement, inventory and customer acceptance consume cash before invoices are collected. A single accounting segment does not mean all products have identical margins. [S01 business overview; S04 business section]

Management reports FY2026 mix of54.68% electrical control panels and40.44% mechanical assemblies, with medical technology only0.63%; the remaining activity includes wire harnesses. These are management product categories, not separately audited segment profits. Three Pune-area facilities and approximately15,800square metres of facilities are described; capacity descriptions do not establish utilization or sellable units. Relationships named in primary disclosures include Atlas Copco, GE, Wabtec, Otis, Kirloskar and Philips. Their presence supports real qualifications but does not guarantee orders or payment. [S01 narrative; S04 business/customer sections]

Revenue is reported net of GST. The revenue note first lists gross product/service lines and subtracts GST; adding those gross lines to reported sales would overstate revenue. Revenue less raw materials, traded purchases and inventory movement is an analytical value-added subtotal, not a fully costed gross profit: factory labor, power and rent also sit in employee/other expense. Export revenue is a minority of total activity. No unverified contract asset, software-like recurring revenue or medical-device annuity is manufactured for the thesis. [S01 notes22–30; S05]

## 5. Moat / Industry Position

The plausible advantage is customer qualification, product engineering and the inconvenience of requalifying a dependable supplier. The economic test is whether that yields retention, price discipline, working-capital terms and attractive capital returns, not merely a recognizable customer logo. Top-five customer concentration was93.08% inFY2023,90.45% inFY2022 and90.57% inFY2021. The prospectus describes substantial purchase-order business without long-term commitments and risks of cancellation or specification changes. Current comprehensive customer and supplier concentration, related-counterparty attribution and cancellation compensation remain ND. [E06; S04 risk/business sections]

An entrant needs machinery, engineering staff, customer audits and a credible delivery record, but neither exclusive IP nor an independently measured dominant market share was established. Customers can dual-source, delay qualification or shift production. The FY2025 downturn despite established relationships is evidence against treating qualifications as guaranteed demand. Raw-material and foreign-currency costs can be passed through only to the extent allowed by actual contracts; no universal price-escalation right is assumed.

## 6. Revenue Growth & Scale

The chosen historical measurement window is FY2021–FY2026: six standalone observations across five intervals. Revenue recognition/perimeter is sufficiently consistent for reported sales arithmetic, although prelisting original audit reports and volume/price decomposition remain incomplete. The prospectus’s restated revenue and later comparative sales agree for overlapping years. Reported growth therefore receives a Medium-confidence score, rather than treating all old operations as nonexistent merely because listing occurred later. [S01–S05]

The five-year result lies in the framework’s10–15% CAGR band, givingREV6 without an extra adjustment. The three-year contraction is equally important and is not replaced by a favorable forecast. Annual sales were ₹59.7739,₹91.5778,₹122.0582,₹121.8503,₹92.4311 and ₹115.5064 crore. Annual additions were ₹31.8039,₹30.4804,negative ₹0.2079,negative ₹29.4192 and ₹23.0753 crore. Ten-year CAGR is ND, not inferred from incorporation age. Early-period pandemic/base effects are a limitation, not a reason to choose whichever window produces the desired score.

FY2026’s25% recovery follows a roughly24% decline inFY2025. H1FY2026 operating sales were ₹58.3126 crore versus a calculated ₹44.4568 crore inH1FY2025, while H2FY2026 was ₹57.1938 crore versus ₹47.9743 crore. Both halves grew year-on-year, but H2 did not exceed H1. There is no extraREV point for a single recovery year after a deep decline. The acquisition contributes no FY2026 revenue and is not treated as organic parent growth. [S05]

Management attributes business changes to OEM schedules, project execution, product mix and qualification timing, including wind-sector demand. A complete volume×price×mix×currency bridge is not disclosed. The value-added cross-check and operating margin expansion show that growth is not solely a mechanical increase in input pass-through, but do not quantify market-share gains. A large asserted order pipeline is not recognized revenue.

## 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway

Existing industrial-control and rail/mechanical customer qualifications offer plausible adjacent demand. The accessible opportunity is the amount these customers can actually award, qualify, schedule and pay for, not a global medical/electrical TAM. The company has invested heavily in facilities, so an early ramp may use spare capacity. However, neither utilization by product nor a coherent installed-units×selling-price bridge was verified. The analysis therefore uses a constrained revenue/capital path rather than inventing units or market share. [E06–E07, E10]

The conditional base case grows FY2026 revenue12% annually, uses18% core EBITDA margin and requires85-day closing receivables, inventory19% of sales, supplier advances0.4%, other operating assets5%, payables9% and accruals2.1%. Operating fixed capital is not allowed to vanish: after using opening spare capacity, the target is65% of annual sales, with maintenance4.5% and D&A4.1% of sales. This is an analyst scenario, not verified capacity or a management commitment. The bull uses22% growth,20% margin and better collections; the bear links lost volume,10% margin,105-day collections and25% inventory with creditor/guarantee stress. [E15; model_inputs.json]

Opening operating IC is approximately ₹136.01 crore, including net fixed assets/CWIP, paid capital advances, operating deposits and ONWC, while the financial-capital proxy has materially expanded sinceFY2023. NOPAT growth has not matched that increase. The three-/five-year numerator, denominator and proxy return are shown above, with limitations on mature-capacity timing, non-operating assets and historical cash presentation. The range of17–20% nominal capital cost used for base/stress is analytical; the15% bull rate is not proof of a low cost of capital.

At current economics, growth consumes substantial operating capital. High growth, large distributions and low new funding cannot all coexist simply because plant was recently built. The growth≈reinvestment×incremental-return identity is a consistency check, not an equation forcing attractive returns. CAP remainsNS because project maturity and the material target acquisition cannot be reconciled, not because a rough proxy was rounded to a low integer. GQS consequently remainsNS; no new-order or small-cap bonus is added.

## 8. Management, Governance & Execution

The Latkar family controls the issuer. The March2026 audited share note and May2026 EGM notice identify promoter holdings around74.82% before the share swap, with the EGM table showing13,210,100 shares. If unchanged, that count would represent about67.17% of current enlarged capital, not74.82%. This is a mechanical conditional calculation, not a verified current ownership filing. A complete post-allotment shareholding/encumbrance record was not retrieved; current pledge percentage is ND, not zero. [S01 note1; S06; S08–S09]

FY2026 remuneration disclosed for Aniket, Chitra and Mayuri Latkar totals ₹2.9711 crore, about24% ofPAT, versus approximately ₹2.958 crore inFY2025. Related-party loans are small, roughly ₹0.0443 crore; related rents and deposits are disclosed separately. The remuneration burden warrants scrutiny, especially in weaker years, but a family business or disclosed commercial RPT does not establish diversion. Prospectus remuneration and historic related-party disclosures provide context, while current target counterparties and all ultimate relationships need more verification. [E08; S01 note43; S02–S04]

On21 August2026 the board allotted2,010,259new shares at ₹207, an aggregate ₹41.6123613 crore, for2,377,850 shares of Laxmi Engineering Industries Bhopal Private Limited. This is noncash consideration: no ₹41.61 crore is added to the cash runway. The new shares increase the denominator by11.39%, with pre-existing holders’ percentage interest falling by about10.22% absent other trades. NSE’s11 September in-principle letter and the19 October active security master corroborate the enlarged capital. No unverified warrant, option or convertible proceeds are invented. [E01, E09; S06–S09]

The valuation report is not target financial assurance. It values the whole target at ₹121.67 crore using75% DCF,15% comparable-company and10% NAV weight; its NAV equity is ₹39.38 crore. Forecast EBIT rises from roughly ₹1.97 crore inFY2027 to ₹20.75 crore inFY2030 while forecast capex is zero and the first projected year releases working capital. Those are aggressive assumptions requiring challenge, not a safe base case. The final acquired share count divided by the valuer’s6,954,250total shares is34.1928%, versus advertised34.41%; the final cap-table discrepancy remains open. The standalone valuation separately tests zero, approximately ₹13.465 crore attributable NAV and ₹41.612 crore issue consideration for the stake, without attributing unverified target cash dividends. [S07 pp2–5,17–25; S08]

Subtracting an unverified target “fair value” while also adding forecast target earnings would double count. The explicit model begins at31 March2026, not with invented October cash. Seven dated slices roll forward April to19 October; operating flows in that interval are assumptions, while the21 August share swap is a known noncash event. Each five-year path then contains60monthly periods and intraperiod payment/collection events. Thirty percent of capex is front-loaded, with repeated supplier payments before collections. The ₹0.25 crore minimum operating buffer is an analytical floor; payment ordering and20cycles/month are assumptions tested against two cycles and80% front funding. A first cash breach is irreversible for valuation purposes even if later arithmetic cash recovers. [model_engine.py; model_inputs.json]

Cost assumptions are calibrated to actual components. FY2026 material/trading/stock cost is ₹64.2323 crore, employee ₹18.7121 and other operating expense ₹10.3429. No loss tax benefit or carryforward is modeled, and same-period new-draw interest and modeled one-off losses receive no tax deduction. ## 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path

The strongest bear case is not that the company lacks real factories or customers. It is that customer concentration and qualification delays leave recently installed capacity underused, while inventory and receivables continue to consume funds. Lower volume then compresses margin, slower collections consume the small available-cash buffer, and capital/term obligations arrive before the next order. A guarantee call, loss of tax-credit access or cash-credit recall can force expensive recapitalization. Even a real plant can be a poor equity investment if its cash returns cannot support the price. [E05–E07, E10–E15]

The single most important thesis variable is cash-producing utilization of the installed asset base: a customer-approved shipment must become collected margin at an acceptable incremental capital cost. Failure here connects demand, earnings and finance rather than treating them as unrelated risks. The minority investment adds a separate permanent-loss route: forecasts embedded in the swap price may not translate into distributable cash or minority realizable value. Neither stake book cost nor the valuer’sDCF is a recovery guarantee.

Impairment risk is High at the stated reference price. Credible modeled stress breaches liquidity even under finite optional financing, so a precise surviving bear equity price would be misleading. The underlying business may continue through refinancing or new equity, but original holders can suffer dilution and value loss. The counterargument is meaningful: FY2026 margin and CFO improved, debt/EBITDA is not extreme, and spare factory capacity could unlock growth without repeating the historical capex rate. This report preserves that upside rather than declaring a model failure to be proven insolvency.

## 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility

At ₹377,5×and10×require ₹1,885 and ₹3,770 per share before distributions, not merely5×or10×revenue. Required price CAGR is37.97%/58.49% over five years and17.46%/25.89% over ten years. These are mathematical requirements, not price targets. Dilution, cash retained for operations, debt and the minority stake must all enter the equity bridge. [multibagger_tests.json]

All four5×/10×and five-/ten-year tests use the same cash engine and finite financing boundaries. Higher revenue requires more inventory, receivables, plant and reserve; it is never funded by an unlimited negative cash balance. Failed growth trials remain in the canonical ledger and produceNSrather than a false multiplier. Lower3×/4×/5×and broader8×/10×/12×terminalEV/EBIT cross-checks use earned operating profit, subtract claims once and share the same survival conditions. No multiple is assigned merely because the present multiple is high.

A large opportunity in rail, electrical equipment or a target company does not establish the required accessible market share. Neither product-level capacity nor a verified target earnings path supports the necessary scale by cutoff. The outcome is Speculative / unsupported, not evidence-backed multibagger potential. A future successful ramp could change that classification; it would need collected margins, funded reinvestment and per-share progress rather than a larger order announcement.

## 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action

Hold — unresolved is the gate-led conclusion. This is neither a numerical buy/sell instruction nor a claim that Saakshi is fraudulent or already insolvent. The record cannot be labeled an evidence-backed compounder: material factors areNS, customer dependence is high, incremental capital economics are not established and the base return is not supported. Gate holds precede the classification matrix; NS bounds do not create a favorable middle score.

Action category: research priority only after the identified reconciliation, capital-allocation and funding evidence is supplied. A more attractive price would improve potential returns but would not establish the target’s audited economics, restore liquidity or clear a financial-reliability hold. For an existing owner, liquidity and company-specific financing exposure need review at the actual holding size before considering any exit implementation; no holdings, tax basis or portfolio weights were supplied.

The most useful favorable update would combine three facts: sales exceeding the former peak with collected margins, a funded operating/maturity plan that does not require an assumed rescue, and defensible per-share returns on the new plant and minority investment. A promotional forecast or stock-price rise alone would not change BQS/GQS. Git/site publication and universe-level completion are outside this company artifact.

sections.content_markdown: Saakshi is principally an OEM control-panel and mechanical-assembly manufacturer, not a predominantly medical-device business. FY2026 revenue recovered to ₹115.51 crore and core EBITDA to ₹22.22 crore, but sales remain below FY2023 while manufacturing capital has expanded substantially. The ₹377 last observed traded close, dated16 October rather than the19 October market cutoff, implies about ₹741.4 crore equity value on the enlarged share count. A material minority acquisition was paid for with shares, not cash. Capital efficiency, the target’s audited economics, historical cash-flow discrepancies and practical exit liquidity remain unresolved. Classification: Hold — unresolved; a conditional turnaround/capital-allocation special situation, not an evidence-backed compounder. A verified, self-funding plant ramp and a defensible acquisition return would change the business assessment; a lower price alone would not clear the evidence holds. [E01–E05, E09–E13]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.content_markdown:
Saakshi designs and manufactures electrical control panels, mechanical assemblies, wire harnesses and some medical-related equipment/components. Customers buy qualified, application-specific manufacturing rather than a consumer brand. Engineering, fabrication, assembly, testing and dependable delivery matter, while raw-material procurement, inventory and customer acceptance consume cash before invoices are collected. A single accounting segment does not mean all products have identical margins. [S01 business overview; S04 business section]

Management reports FY2026 mix of54.68% electrical control panels and40.44% mechanical assemblies, with medical technology only0.63%; the remaining activity includes wire harnesses. These are management product categories, not separately audited segment profits. Three Pune-area facilities and approximately15,800square metres of facilities are described; capacity descriptions do not establish utilization or sellable units. Relationships named in primary disclosures include Atlas Copco, GE, Wabtec, Otis, Kirloskar and Philips. Their presence supports real qualifications but does not guarantee orders or payment. [S01 narrative; S04 business/customer sections]

Revenue is reported net of GST. The revenue note first lists gross product/service lines and subtracts GST; adding those gross lines to reported sales would overstate revenue. Revenue less raw materials, traded purchases and inventory movement is an analytical value-added subtotal, not a fully costed gross profit: factory labor, power and rent also sit in employee/other expense. Export revenue is a minority of total activity. No unverified contract asset, software-like recurring revenue or medical-device annuity is manufactured for the thesis. [S01 notes22–30; S05]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.content_markdown:
The plausible advantage is customer qualification, product engineering and the inconvenience of requalifying a dependable supplier. The economic test is whether that yields retention, price discipline, working-capital terms and attractive capital returns, not merely a recognizable customer logo. Top-five customer concentration was93.08% inFY2023,90.45% inFY2022 and90.57% inFY2021. The prospectus describes substantial purchase-order business without long-term commitments and risks of cancellation or specification changes. Current comprehensive customer and supplier concentration, related-counterparty attribution and cancellation compensation remain ND. [E06; S04 risk/business sections]

An entrant needs machinery, engineering staff, customer audits and a credible delivery record, but neither exclusive IP nor an independently measured dominant market share was established. Customers can dual-source, delay qualification or shift production. The FY2025 downturn despite established relationships is evidence against treating qualifications as guaranteed demand. Raw-material and foreign-currency costs can be passed through only to the extent allowed by actual contracts; no universal price-escalation right is assumed.

sections.content_markdown:
The chosen historical measurement window is FY2021–FY2026: six standalone observations across five intervals. Revenue recognition/perimeter is sufficiently consistent for reported sales arithmetic, although prelisting original audit reports and volume/price decomposition remain incomplete. The prospectus’s restated revenue and later comparative sales agree for overlapping years. Reported growth therefore receives a Medium-confidence score, rather than treating all old operations as nonexistent merely because listing occurred later. [S01–S05]

The five-year result lies in the framework’s10–15% CAGR band, givingREV6 without an extra adjustment. The three-year contraction is equally important and is not replaced by a favorable forecast. Annual sales were ₹59.7739,₹91.5778,₹122.0582,₹121.8503,₹92.4311 and ₹115.5064 crore. Annual additions were ₹31.8039,₹30.4804,negative ₹0.2079,negative ₹29.4192 and ₹23.0753 crore. Ten-year CAGR is ND, not inferred from incorporation age. Early-period pandemic/base effects are a limitation, not a reason to choose whichever window produces the desired score.

FY2026’s25% recovery follows a roughly24% decline inFY2025. H1FY2026 operating sales were ₹58.3126 crore versus a calculated ₹44.4568 crore inH1FY2025, while H2FY2026 was ₹57.1938 crore versus ₹47.9743 crore. Both halves grew year-on-year, but H2 did not exceed H1. There is no extraREV point for a single recovery year after a deep decline. The acquisition contributes no FY2026 revenue and is not treated as organic parent growth. [S05]

Management attributes business changes to OEM schedules, project execution, product mix and qualification timing, including wind-sector demand. A complete volume×price×mix×currency bridge is not disclosed. The value-added cross-check and operating margin expansion show that growth is not solely a mechanical increase in input pass-through, but do not quantify market-share gains. A large asserted order pipeline is not recognized revenue.

sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.content_markdown:
Existing industrial-control and rail/mechanical customer qualifications offer plausible adjacent demand. The accessible opportunity is the amount these customers can actually award, qualify, schedule and pay for, not a global medical/electrical TAM. The company has invested heavily in facilities, so an early ramp may use spare capacity. However, neither utilization by product nor a coherent installed-units×selling-price bridge was verified. The analysis therefore uses a constrained revenue/capital path rather than inventing units or market share. [E06–E07, E10]

The conditional base case grows FY2026 revenue12% annually, uses18% core EBITDA margin and requires85-day closing receivables, inventory19% of sales, supplier advances0.4%, other operating assets5%, payables9% and accruals2.1%. Operating fixed capital is not allowed to vanish: after using opening spare capacity, the target is65% of annual sales, with maintenance4.5% and D&A4.1% of sales. This is an analyst scenario, not verified capacity or a management commitment. The bull uses22% growth,20% margin and better collections; the bear links lost volume,10% margin,105-day collections and25% inventory with creditor/guarantee stress. [E15; model_inputs.json]

Opening operating IC is approximately ₹136.01 crore, including net fixed assets/CWIP, paid capital advances, operating deposits and ONWC, while the financial-capital proxy has materially expanded sinceFY2023. NOPAT growth has not matched that increase. The three-/five-year numerator, denominator and proxy return are shown above, with limitations on mature-capacity timing, non-operating assets and historical cash presentation. The range of17–20% nominal capital cost used for base/stress is analytical; the15% bull rate is not proof of a low cost of capital.

At current economics, growth consumes substantial operating capital. High growth, large distributions and low new funding cannot all coexist simply because plant was recently built. The growth≈reinvestment×incremental-return identity is a consistency check, not an equation forcing attractive returns. CAP remainsNS because project maturity and the material target acquisition cannot be reconciled, not because a rough proxy was rounded to a low integer. GQS consequently remainsNS; no new-order or small-cap bonus is added.

sections.title: Management, Governance & Execution
sections.content_markdown:
The Latkar family controls the issuer. The March2026 audited share note and May2026 EGM notice identify promoter holdings around74.82% before the share swap, with the EGM table showing13,210,100 shares. If unchanged, that count would represent about67.17% of current enlarged capital, not74.82%. This is a mechanical conditional calculation, not a verified current ownership filing. A complete post-allotment shareholding/encumbrance record was not retrieved; current pledge percentage is ND, not zero. [S01 note1; S06; S08–S09]

FY2026 remuneration disclosed for Aniket, Chitra and Mayuri Latkar totals ₹2.9711 crore, about24% ofPAT, versus approximately ₹2.958 crore inFY2025. Related-party loans are small, roughly ₹0.0443 crore; related rents and deposits are disclosed separately. The remuneration burden warrants scrutiny, especially in weaker years, but a family business or disclosed commercial RPT does not establish diversion. Prospectus remuneration and historic related-party disclosures provide context, while current target counterparties and all ultimate relationships need more verification. [E08; S01 note43; S02–S04]

On21 August2026 the board allotted2,010,259new shares at ₹207, an aggregate ₹41.6123613 crore, for2,377,850 shares of Laxmi Engineering Industries Bhopal Private Limited. This is noncash consideration: no ₹41.61 crore is added to the cash runway. The new shares increase the denominator by11.39%, with pre-existing holders’ percentage interest falling by about10.22% absent other trades. NSE’s11 September in-principle letter and the19 October active security master corroborate the enlarged capital. No unverified warrant, option or convertible proceeds are invented. [E01, E09; S06–S09]

The valuation report is not target financial assurance. It values the whole target at ₹121.67 crore using75% DCF,15% comparable-company and10% NAV weight; its NAV equity is ₹39.38 crore. Forecast EBIT rises from roughly ₹1.97 crore inFY2027 to ₹20.75 crore inFY2030 while forecast capex is zero and the first projected year releases working capital. Those are aggressive assumptions requiring challenge, not a safe base case. The final acquired share count divided by the valuer’s6,954,250total shares is34.1928%, versus advertised34.41%; the final cap-table discrepancy remains open. The standalone valuation separately tests zero, approximately ₹13.465 crore attributable NAV and ₹41.612 crore issue consideration for the stake, without attributing unverified target cash dividends. [S07 pp2–5,17–25; S08]

Original FY2024–FY2026 audits are unmodified and IFC is reported adequate/effective. sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.content_markdown:
The strongest bear case is not that the company lacks real factories or customers. It is that customer concentration and qualification delays leave recently installed capacity underused, while inventory and receivables continue to consume funds. Lower volume then compresses margin, slower collections consume the small available-cash buffer, and capital/term obligations arrive before the next order. A guarantee call, loss of tax-credit access or cash-credit recall can force expensive recapitalization. Even a real plant can be a poor equity investment if its cash returns cannot support the price. [E05–E07, E10–E15]

The single most important thesis variable is cash-producing utilization of the installed asset base: a customer-approved shipment must become collected margin at an acceptable incremental capital cost. Failure here connects demand, earnings and finance rather than treating them as unrelated risks. The minority investment adds a separate permanent-loss route: forecasts embedded in the swap price may not translate into distributable cash or minority realizable value. Neither stake book cost nor the valuer’sDCF is a recovery guarantee.

Impairment risk is High at the stated reference price. Credible modeled stress breaches liquidity even under finite optional financing, so a precise surviving bear equity price would be misleading. The underlying business may continue through refinancing or new equity, but original holders can suffer dilution and value loss. The counterargument is meaningful: FY2026 margin and CFO improved, debt/EBITDA is not extreme, and spare factory capacity could unlock growth without repeating the historical capex rate. This report preserves that upside rather than declaring a model failure to be proven insolvency.

sections.content_markdown:
At ₹377,5×and10×require ₹1,885 and ₹3,770 per share before distributions, not merely5×or10×revenue. Required price CAGR is37.97%/58.49% over five years and17.46%/25.89% over ten years. These are mathematical requirements, not price targets. Dilution, cash retained for operations, debt and the minority stake must all enter the equity bridge. [multibagger_tests.json]

All four5×/10×and five-/ten-year tests use the same cash engine and finite financing boundaries. Higher revenue requires more inventory, receivables, plant and reserve; it is never funded by an unlimited negative cash balance. Failed growth trials remain in the canonical ledger and produceNSrather than a false multiplier. Lower3×/4×/5×and broader8×/10×/12×terminalEV/EBIT cross-checks use earned operating profit, subtract claims once and share the same survival conditions. No multiple is assigned merely because the present multiple is high.

A large opportunity in rail, electrical equipment or a target company does not establish the required accessible market share. Neither product-level capacity nor a verified target earnings path supports the necessary scale by cutoff. The outcome is Speculative / unsupported, not evidence-backed multibagger potential. A future successful ramp could change that classification; it would need collected margins, funded reinvestment and per-share progress rather than a larger order announcement.

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.content_markdown:
Hold — unresolved is the gate-led conclusion. This is neither a numerical buy/sell instruction nor a claim that Saakshi is fraudulent or already insolvent. The record cannot be labeled an evidence-backed compounder: material factors areNS, customer dependence is high, incremental capital economics are not established and the base return is not supported. Gate holds precede the classification matrix; NS bounds do not create a favorable middle score.

Action category: research priority only after the identified reconciliation, capital-allocation and funding evidence is supplied. A more attractive price would improve potential returns but would not establish the target’s audited economics, restore liquidity or clear a financial-reliability hold. For an existing owner, liquidity and company-specific financing exposure need review at the actual holding size before considering any exit implementation; no holdings, tax basis or portfolio weights were supplied.

The most useful favorable update would combine three facts: sales exceeding the former peak with collected margins, a funded operating/maturity plan that does not require an assumed rescue, and defensible per-share returns on the new plant and minority investment. A promotional forecast or stock-price rise alone would not change BQS/GQS. Git/site publication and universe-level completion are outside this company artifact.
